title: Plane-wave propagation in vacuum and in a uniform n=1.5 dielectric, 2D and 3D, against the exact Yee dispersion relation and the continuum

fixture.engine: torchfdtd.boundaries.YeeGrid update_E/update_H (part A) and torchfdtd.Simulation (part B); staircase, uniform mesh, courant_factor 0.99 (c dt/h = 0.99/sqrt(2) in 2D, 0.99/sqrt(3) in 3D)

part_A_eigenmode.description: all-periodic cell, E initialised to the real discrete plane wave with amplitude vector orthogonal to the discrete wavevector K_a = 2 sin(k_a h/2)/h, H = 0; cos(omega dt) measured from the three-term recurrence E[n+1]+E[n-1] = 2 cos(omega dt) E[n] over every cell after 3 steps; polarization purity measured after 40 steps

mesh_sweep.wavevector: (2 pi / (N h), 0, 0): one wavelength across the periodic x axis
(2 pi / (N h), 0, 0): one wavelength across the periodic x axis
(2 pi / (N h), 0, 0): one wavelength across the periodic x axis

oblique.wavevector: q = 2 pi m / N per axis with m = (1, -2, 1) (m_z = 0 in 2D)

two_d: TM: E in-plane orthogonal to K

part_A_eigenmode.wavelength_definition: part A fixes k; N = cells per wavelength 2 pi / k in the medium

part_B_propagation.description: pulsed sheet source, two point monitors on the propagation axis at a fixed physical separation, phase difference of the +f DFT of the raw traces gives k_measured(f) D; the run ends before the far-end PML echo (the only -x wave) can reach the second monitor; the near-end echo travels +x and is consistent with the measurement

source.note: one-cycle Gaussian at 193.4 THz with the C1 endpoint taper so the drive starts at exactly zero; amplitude 1; soft sheet (radiates both ways)

part_B_propagation.steps: round(100 fs / dt) at each mesh
part_B_propagation.wavelength_definition: part B fixes the vacuum wavelength 1.55 um; in the dielectric the material wavelength has N/1.5 cells

layer_A.description: part B fixture at N=20 rerun on CUDA FP32 with the CUDA graph, 2D TE vacuum and 3D Ey dielectric; raw traces divided by the FP64 peak are compared to the CPU FP64 traces

reference_method: exact Yee dispersion relation (n/(c dt))^2 sin^2(omega dt/2) = sum_a sin^2(k_a h/2)/h^2, written in the test; continuum omega = c |k| / n; both evaluated in the test, no solver code

observables.name: cos_omega_dt_residual
observables.definition: |cos(omega dt) from the recurrence - cos(omega dt) from the Yee relation| per part-A case

observables.name: polarization_leak
observables.definition: max |E - (E.pol) pol| / max |E| after 40 steps (part A)

observables.name: phase_error_per_wavelength
observables.definition: 2 pi (k_measured / k_continuum - 1) (part B) and 2 pi (k_Yee / k_continuum - 1) (prediction)

observables.name: phase_residual_vs_yee
observables.definition: |k_measured - k_Yee| D at each of the 11 frequencies (part B)

observables.name: trace_end_over_peak
observables.definition: |trace at the last step| / max |trace| at monitor b (window-truncation floor, part B)

observables.name: polarization_trace_difference
observables.definition: max |trace(pol 1) - trace(pol 2)| / peak, 2D TE vs TM and 3D Ey vs Ez (identical discrete problems by grid symmetry)

observables.name: layer_A_trace_error
observables.definition: CUDA FP32 trace / FP64 peak against CPU FP64 trace / FP64 peak

part_A_discrete_relation.note: round-off level in FP64; the relation is exact, so any mesh passes

part_B_discrete_relation.note: not round-off: window truncation and the C1 taper set the floor; the continuum error is 3.3e-3 rad per vacuum wavelength at N=40 (6.6e-3 over D) and larger at coarser meshes, so 1e-3 separates the two

continuum.policy: reported only; the continuum phase error is the numerical dispersion of the scheme, expected to fall by about 4x per mesh halving; no pass/fail

acceptance.source_of_limits: COMPLETION_PROGRAM_KO.md section 5 (discrete forward tolerances); the round-off tolerances are this case's own pre-declared budget

notes: The N=40 meshes of part B (2D and 3D) run only when TORCHFDTD_G3_FINE=1; the recorded run sets it. tests/test_boundaries.py::test_discrete_plane_wave_eigenmode already checks the vacuum eigenmode with H initialised; this case adds the dielectric, both 3D polarizations, the mesh sweep, the continuum error and the Simulation path.
